Here’s How You Can Track Your 2026 Midterm Election Ballots

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:55
Instaread

Posted by: Alexandra Ines in Community News, Santa Clarita Latest News October 18, 2026 - 3:45 pm 0 495 Views

As the November Election Day creeps closer, there are multiple ways for Santa Clarita residents to ensure their ballot has been counted.

Mail-in ballots have already been issued to California residents at the beginning of this month; letting individuals to vote early.

According to California Secretary of State Shirley N. Weber, it is recommended that mail-in ballots are sent 5 days before election day, which in this period is on October 30.

If voters decide to personally deliver their ballots, they must be delivered to a polling place or ballot box by the close of polls at 8 PM on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. 

Voters can use the  “Where’s My Ballot?” website, hosted by the California Secretary of State, to track the status of their ballots leading up to election day. This service allows voters the opportunity to be notified when their ballots are mailed, received, and counted.

If you still need to register to vote, register online on the State Website.

Los Angeles County residents can also check their ballot status on the L.A. Vote website.

For more information about election day voting, check out the California Secretary of State website HERE.

About Alexandra Ines

Born and raised in the Santa Clarita Valley, Alexandra Ines has lived there since she was six months old. Her love for news and filmmaking started when she was young but was elevated with education. As a first step, she was accepted for the morning broadcast show, La Mesa Live, at La Mesa Junior High School. After her 2 years of exceptional work in the program, Alexandra was awarded the Outstanding Achievement in Video Production. She was quickly accepted into the prestigious Golden Valley Television (GVTV) at Golden Valley High School. In four years, Alexandra mastered numerous live broadcast skills, including crafting interviews and news segments. Most notably, she produced, filmed, and edited her very own baking show having a total of 12 episodes under her belt. In her junior year, she was given the mantle of the program’s producer, serving as a creative and informed leader for her team. Alexandra and a group of her peers created PSA videos on distracted driving and DUI awareness which lead to gaining 5 awards over 2 videos for the Streets Art SAFE Competition. Alexandra received her associate’s degree in filmmaking at College of the Canyons and is currently studying at California State University, Northridge as a film major with an emphasis in film editing. In Alexandra's role at KHTS, she edits news videos to serve as visual media for viewers. Alexandra spends her free time collecting and listening to her vinyl records and continues to bake outside of her baking show. She also enjoys travelling either by herself or with friends and occasionally going to live concerts.

How this consent management platform (CMP) works:

CMP privacy choices

Storage, duration, and usage details

The choices you make with this CMP regarding the purposes and entities will affect how personalized advertising is presented to you. We need to store these choices to respect them on future visits, and they are stored differently based on the type of site or app you're using:
  • For sites, your choices are saved in a cookie named “FCCDCF” for a maximum duration of 390 days.
  • For apps, your choices are saved in device storage prefixed by “IABTCF_”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this app.
  • For accelerated mobile page (AMP) sites, your choices are saved in local storage prefixed by “amp-store”. Your choices will be invalidated after 390 days and overwritten once you make new privacy choices on this site.
